__
 
• The sentence structure implies a condition that did not occur in the past, which is a situation for third conditional (also known as 'Counterfactual' conditional).
 
• In the third conditional, the structure is usually: If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle.
 
• Hence 'I had got an opportunity' forms the correct phrase in this context.

**Therefore, the correct answer is- "Option 3'.**

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

The hypothesis had been thoroughly tested by the scientist before it was presented.

options.text: The scientist had thoroughly tested the hypothesis before he presented it.
The scientist thoroughly tested the hypothesis before it was presenting.
The scientist thoroughly tested the hypothesis before he was presenting it.
The scientist had thoroughly testing the hypothesis before presenting it.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**The scientist had thoroughly tested the hypothesis before he presented it.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence given in the question is in** Passive Voice**, and the task is to convert it into **Active Voice.**
 
• The sentence is structured in the **past perfect tense**.
 
 
• **Passive Voice **takes the format: **Subject + had been + V3 + by + agent.**
 
• **Active Voice,** on the other hand, uses: **Subject (agent) + had + V3 + Object.**
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• **Passive Voice: **"The marathon **had been completed** by them."

 
 
• **Active voice: **"They **had completed **the marathon."
 
 
 
 
 
• In the given sentence,** 'the hypothesis'** is the object and '**the scientist'** is the agent.
 
• This is reversed in the Active Voice, where** 'the scientist' **becomes the **subject **and '**the hypothesis**' becomes the **object**.
 
• The verb phrase **'had been thoroughly tested'** is transformed into **'had thoroughly tested' **in **Active Voice**, keeping the** past perfect tense** intact.
 
• With these transformations, the Passive sentence "The hypothesis had been thoroughly tested by the scientist before it was presented" becomes "**The scientist had thoroughly tested the hypothesis before he presented it"** in Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of the zones of a pond ecosystem from the bottom to top?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Option 1__.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct sequence of the zones of a pond ecosystem from the bottom to top is **Hypolimnion-Thermocline-Epilimnion.**
 
• Hypolimnion: The hypolimnion is the bottom layer of a pond or lake. It is characterized by lower temperatures and typically has minimal mixing with the upper layers. 
 
 
• This zone often contains colder, denser water and is less influenced by surface temperature changes.
 
 
 
• Thermocline: The thermocline is the middle layer where a rapid temperature change occurs. It acts as a barrier between the warmer upper layer (epilimnion) and the colder lower layer (hypolimnion). 
 
 
• The thermocline is a region where temperature decreases rapidly with depth.
 
 
 
• Littoral: The littoral zone is the top layer of a pond or lake, extending from the shoreline to the open water area. 
 
 
• It is the shallow, nearshore region where sunlight penetrates to the bottom, supporting the growth of aquatic plants. 
 
• This zone is often rich in biodiversity and provides important habitat for various organisms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A pond ecosystem consists of various zones, each characterized by different environmental conditions and supporting distinct communities of organisms. 
 
• The main zones of a pond ecosystem, from the bottom to the top, are as follows:
 
 
• 
 
Benthic Zone:

 
 
• 
 
​Description: The benthic zone is the bottom layer of the pond, comprising the sediment and substrate. It can include mud, sand, rocks, and organic matter.

 
 
• 
 
Organisms: Benthic organisms include various bottom-dwelling invertebrates such as worms, insect larvae, and crustaceans. Some fish species may also forage in this zone.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
​Hypolimnion: 

 
 
• 
 
​Description: The hypolimnion is the deep, colder layer of the pond located below the thermocline. It remains thermally stratified and less affected by surface temperature changes.

 
 
• 
 
Temperature: The temperature in the hypolimnion is relatively constant and lower than in the epilimnion.

 
 
• 
 
Organisms: Some cold-water fish species and deep-water invertebrates may inhabit this zone.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
Thermocline:

 
 
• 
 
​Description: The thermocline is a transitional layer between the warmer upper layer (epilimnion) and the colder lower layer (hypolimnion). It is characterized by a rapid temperature change with depth.

 
 
• 
 
Temperature: The temperature decreases quickly with depth in the thermocline.

 
 
• 
 
Organisms: The thermocline may influence the distribution of plankton and fish, as it marks a temperature transition.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
Epilimnion:

 
 
• 
 
​Description: The epilimnion is the upper layer of the pond, extending from the surface to the thermocline. It is influenced by sunlight and mixing due to wind, leading to relatively uniform temperatures.

 
 
• 
 
Temperature: The temperature is warmer in the epilimnion, and sunlight penetration supports photosynthesis.

 
 
• 
 
Organisms: This zone supports a variety of phytoplankton, aquatic plants, and fish species. It is often rich in biodiversity.

 
 
 
 
• **Littoral Zone**:
 
 
• **​Description**: The littoral zone is the shallow, nearshore area of the pond where light penetrates to the bottom. It includes the area from the shoreline to the point where rooted plants no longer grow.
 
• **Organisms**: The littoral zone supports a diverse range of aquatic plants, algae, and a variety of invertebrates. It is an important habitat for amphibians, insects, and smaller fish.

questions.question: In land grants inscriptions of Gupta period the term ‘Akshaya-nivi' refers to -

options.text: Donee have right over the land for a specific period.
Donee have right over the land for two generations.
Donee have full right over the land and can sell it to others.
Donee can only enjoy the production of the land but can not sell the land.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is: 'Donee can only enjoy the production of the land but can not sell the land.'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **The term 'Akshaya-nivi' in Gupta period inscriptions refers to a type of land grant where the donee could only enjoy the produce of the land but did not have the right to sell the land.**

 
 
• This statement is **correct.**
 
• The concept of 'Akshaya-nivi' ensured that the ownership of the land remained with the donor, while the donee had the right to use the land for cultivation and other productive purposes.
 
• Such grants were typically made to Brahmins, temples, and other religious institutions to support their sustenance without transferring full ownership.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Incorrect Options__**

__
 
• **Donee have right over the land for a specific period.**

 
 
• This statement is **incorrect.**
 
• Land grants with specific periods were different from 'Akshaya-nivi' grants, which were intended to be permanent as long as the land was used productively.
 
 
 
• **Donee have right over the land for two generations.**
 
 
• This statement is **incorrect.**
 
• 'Akshaya-nivi' did not limit the rights to two generations; it was meant to be a perpetual grant for the donee's usage.
 
 
 
• **Donee have full right over the land and can sell it to others.**
 
 
• This statement is **incorrect.**
 
• 'Akshaya-nivi' did not confer the right to sell the land; the donee could only utilize the land for its produce.
 
 

**Hence, the correct interpretation of 'Akshaya-nivi' is that the donee can only enjoy the production of the land but cannot sell the land.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

 __
 
• Land grants were a common practice during the Gupta period, often given to Brahmins, religious institutions, and officials as a reward or for sustaining religious activities.
 
• These grants were recorded on copper plates and inscriptions, detailing the rights and limitations associated with the grants.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Social Implications:**__
 
 
• The system of land grants helped in the expansion of agricultural activities and the establishment of new settlements.
 
• It also played a role in the consolidation of Brahminical influence and the spread of religious practices, as many grants were made to Brahmins and temples.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD):

1. IOD develops in the equatorial region of Indian Ocean from April to May peaking in October.

2. Positive IOD is good for Indian Monsoons.

Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Indian Ocean Dipole is a recently discovered phenomenon that has a significant influence on Indian monsoons.**

 
• Indian Ocean Dipole is an SST anomaly (Sea Surface Temperature Anomaly – different from normal) that occurs occasionally in the Northern or Equatorial Indian Ocean Region (IOR).
 
• The Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) is defined by the difference in sea surface temperature between two areas (or poles, hence a dipole) – **a western pole in the Arabian Sea (western Indian Ocean)** and an **eastern pole in the eastern Indian Ocean south of Indonesia**.
 
• IOD develops in the equatorial region of Indian Ocean from April to May **peaking in October**. ***Hence Statement 1 is correct.***
 
• With positive IOD, winds over the Indian Ocean blow from east to west (from Bay of Bengal towards the Arabian Sea).
 
• This results in the Arabian Sea (the western Indian Ocean near the African Coast) being much warmer and eastern Indian Ocean around Indonesia becoming colder and dry.
 
• In the negative dipole year, the reverse happens to make Indonesia much warmer and rainier.
 
• In essence, a** positive IOD leads to greater monsoon rainfall** and more active (above normal rainfall) monsoon days in Indian sub-continent. ***Hence Statement 2 is correct.***
 
• While negative IOD leads to less rainfall and more monsoon break days (no rainfall).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/84bdab2ceb7d979d9c8bcb4b8b7da454eab1c1c20b79118465a10fcc7d469e1a.png]

• Somaliland, officially known as the Republic of Somaliland, is an **unrecognized state in the Horn of Africa. *Hence option 1 is the correct answer.***

• It is** located on the southern coast of the Gulf of Aden and is bordered by Djibouti to the northwest, Ethiopia to the south and west, and Somalia to the east.**
 
• The capital and largest city of Somaliland is** Hargeisa.**
 
• The official languages are **Somali and Arabic, **with English also being spoken. 
 
• The Government of Somaliland regards itself as the** successor state to British Somaliland**, which, as the briefly independent State of Somaliland, united from 1960 to 1991 with the Trust Territory of Somaliland (the former Italian Somaliland) to form the Somali Republic.
 
• Since 1991, the territory has been governed by **democratically elected governments** that seek international recognition as the government of the Republic of Somaliland.
 
• However, Somaliland’s self-proclaimed independence has not been officially recognised by any UN member state or international organisation.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Indian Judiciary?

1. There can be a single High Court for two or more States

2. Union Territories cannot have their own High Court

3. Powers to remove the Chief Justice of a High Court are vested in the Governor

Which of the above statements is/are not true
questions.solution:
**Statements 2 and 3 are not true** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 231 of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of a common High Court for two or more States.
 
• According to Article 214 of the Constitution, there is a provision for a High Court for every State.
 
• A judge serving in any High Court of India is removed by the President only on the basis of majority received by both the Houses.
 
• Some Union Territories have their own High Court 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial court in India and the final court of appeal under the Indian Constitution, as well as the highest constitutional court with judicial review power.
 
• India is a federal state with a unified legal system comprised of three tiers: the Supreme Court, High Courts, and Subordinate Courts.
 
• The Indian constitution has a Supreme Court clause in Part V (The Union) and Chapter 6 (The Union Judiciary).
 
• Part V of the Constitution, Articles 124 to 147, deal with the Supreme Court's organization, independence, jurisdiction, powers, and procedures.
 
• According to Article 124(1) of the Indian constitution, there shall be a Supreme Court of India consisting of a Chief Justice of India (CJI) and not more than seven additional Judges unless Parliament by law mandates a larger number.

 The Supreme Court of India's jurisdiction can be divided into three categories: original jurisdiction, appellate jurisdiction, and advisory jurisdiction. The Supreme Court does, however, have additional authorities.
